title: Retry with backoff
subtitle: A finite, invented example — nothing is executed
intro: Follow the failed attempts through waits of 1, 2 and 4 seconds. Any successful attempt ends immediately. A fourth failure ends the attempt sequence.
ask: Are the retry limit and both outcomes clear?
afterwards: Your comments will guide a revised explanation; this page sends no requests and runs no retries.

items.title: The waits grow but the number of attempts is finite
items.body: This illustration tries once, then retries at most three times after waits of 1, 2 and 4 seconds. Real systems also need policies for retryable failures, idempotency, deadlines and jitter; these invented numbers are not a production recommendation.

items.title: Success and exhaustion both have an outcome
items.body: Success returns the result. Exhausting four attempts reports failure and leaves the caller to choose what to do next; it does not silently restart.
